newsitem.title: ISRAEL: RESEARCH ALERT: Discount Invest a buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT: Discount Invest a buy.

text.p: Israel's Discount Investment Corp, a holding company, remains a buy and should show improved results over the coming quarters, Sahar Securities said in a research report released on Sunday.

"In our opinion, the coming quarterly results will be better than the results of the first nine months of 1996, mainly because of a continued improvement in the results of its Supersol, Property & Building Corp and telecommunications companies," analyst Boaz Levitan said.

Levitan retained his buy recommendation for Discount and set a target price of 240-275 shekels a share. He based his forecast on projected 1997 earnings of 23.5 shekels a share and a target price-to-earnings ratio of 11. Sahar estimated 1996 per share earnings would be 16.5 shekels.
Discount closed on Sunday at 204.97 shekels.
Levitan warned that Discount was exposed to the cyclical building sector and that further write-offs at Scitex Ltd should be expected but at lower levels than in the third quarter.
Sahar said it expected to see some improvements in Clal Israel, in which Discount has a 6.7 percent holding, because the conglomerate was undergoing a change in management.
"It is difficult to estimate what the overall effect of the stable cleaning will be but shareholders must be ready for a 'flood' of one-time clauses in Clal Group results," Levitan said.

Sahar said that despite the high penetration rate in Israel's cellular communications market, there is still growth potential for Discount's Cellcom affiliate, one of the country's two mobile phone operators.
Levitan noted that Cellcom was due to double tariffs as of January 1 and impose a user fee.
